lane: buried-structure: basement-depth steps from gravity inversion
hypothesis: A buried normal fault is a MONOPOLE step in the GP-1012-calibrated inverted basement surface: the depth offset persists along the gradient direction, whereas the lane's named competing explanation -- density contrasts inside the basement -- closes into a dipole.  Additionally, a step seen by BOTH the lane's band-13 inversion and the organiser-supplied band-15 depth surface (independent processing chains) is less likely to be an inversion artefact.
mechanism: Isostatic residual gravity (band 13) -> Parker/Oldenburg slab inversion at 200 m, regional removed at 15 km, density contrast calibrated to GP-1012 basin-depth statistics -> Blakely-Simpson maxima of |grad depth| with measured throw >= 80 m -> (E2) far-field/near-field offset persistence along the local gradient on the locally-detrended depth surface; (E3) mutual +/-5 px corridor agreement with band-15 depth-surface steps -> dots at 3 px spacing in the basin interior, pruned >2-3 px from the visible mapped catalogue.
named_non_fault_process: Density contrasts within basement (sills, dikes, pluton flanks, intrabasement lithologic contacts) make the same horizontal-gradient maximum.  E2 measures the discriminator directly: a finite body's offset closes over +/-800 m (far/near < 0.6 or sign flip); a fault's offset persists.  E3's independent-depth consensus is the second, unrelated filter.

experiments.E1_baseline: T0 arm: pure lane field re-measured on the current evaluator
experiments.E3_consensus: T2 arm: band-13 inversion x band-15 supplied depth consensus
